commits.message:
docs, tests: the drill and pin prose says what the tree does; one drill recipient redirect

operations.md: the state-backend pins row names what is pinned —
`settings.POSTGRES_IMAGE` and `settings.AGE_VERSION`, each moved by a
renovate custom manager on the settings file — what an age bump still
needs by hand, and cites the sections that describe the pins. The two
sentences that said the ops repository carries no workflow now say what
it carries (`lint.yml`, `probes.yml`), why neither reads the drill key,
that no job there starts until the repository's Actions billing is
restored (kluster-ops#393), and, per drill, why the rest do not run.

cluster-infra.md: `update_crds/pins.py` is not the stack's chart pin
register; the stack reads `versions:chart-<name>` from `Pulumi.yaml`,
nothing holds the two equal, and a chart bump is a Renovate-opened pin
edit plus a hand edit to `pins.py` and a regeneration. Neither the pins
nor their manager exist yet (kluster-ops#249).

tests: `drill_recipient_redirect.redirect` holds the one body both
`drill_recipient_file` fixtures used to repeat; each fixture calls it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KP8SoeYJnEdAuVNJpHFvQa

docs, tests: the drill's status says why it has not run; the orphan audit is in-cluster

state-backend.md §1 and §7.3 gave "the ops repository carries no
workflows" as why no drill pass has happened. The drill's workflow is
not written (kluster-ops#57), and no job in that repository starts until
its Actions billing is restored (kluster-ops#393).

deploy/state-backend/README.md: the §7.3.1 rehearsal ran on 2026-09-18
(kluster-ops#281) and the first production replace-and-restore on
2026-09-25 (kluster-ops#385). What stays unproven is opening, with the
kit, an object the appliance uploaded itself, and the drill key's
`--identity-file` restore.

operations.md: the orphan-volume audit is an in-cluster drill, per the
ruling recorded on kluster-ops#57 — it compares each node's on-disk
volume directories against the live volumes — so its row and the
exceptions list say so.

tests/test_dump_and_restore.py: "artefact" is spelled "artifact".

docs: the restore path's status says what ran and what is unproven

state-backend.md's introduction and §7.3.1, and credentials.md's
recovery-chain bullet, said `state-backend restore` had never run
against a live box. The §7.3.1 rehearsal ran steps 2 to 9 on
2026-09-18 against a scratch box, on a workstation dump
(kluster-ops#281), and the appliance's first replace-and-restore ran
the restore against production on 2026-09-25 (kluster-ops#385). What
neither proved is opening, with the kit, an object the appliance
uploaded itself, and so step 1 as written. No drill has run.

docs: ci.md says which form of the state-backend rebuild has run

The rebuild playbook was "written down, never run". Its scheduled drill
(physical/state-backend.md §7.3) has never run; its operator form
(§7.3.1) ran against a scratch box on 2026-09-18, and `state-backend
restore` ran against the appliance in its first replace-and-restore on
2026-09-25.
